title: How an AI Agent Decides Which Tool to Call  #aiautomation #techtok
description:
One of the most interesting things about AI agents is how they actually decide which tool to use for which situation.

Every tool inside an agent has metadata attached to it. A short description, a few lines that explain exactly what that tool does. When you ask the agent to draft and send an email, it does not just guess. It scans those descriptions, reads the blurbs, and figures out which tool fits the task without burning through a massive amount of tokens doing it.

The same logic applies to skills. You can build custom skills inside an agent and write a two to three line metadata description at the top that tells the agent exactly when and how to use it. That small addition makes the whole system dramatically more efficient.

The even more interesting part is that because of this infrastructure, something like Claude Code can recognize when no existing tool fits the task and actually suggest how to build one. The agent knows what it has, knows what it does not have, and can flag the gap.
